speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon).

The clinical triad of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium within 48 hours, and abdominal distension in a newborn is highly suggestive of this condition. Given the home birth context and lack of immediate postnatal meconium passage, this is the most likely diagnosis. Please proceed with an abdominal X-ray to confirm the absence of meconium and look for a transition zone.
